scope: Competing known armour and close infantry threat priority in existing owner-local tactical assessment. Not complete tacticsAssess parity.
sourceIntent: Reference evaluates nearby tank threat before close indoor infantry assault, with a fast-movement exception. CBE retains its existing authored forward-order policy instead of copying random plan selection or full-group setting writes.
finding: CBE selected fresh close infantry assault before its armour-overmatch branch. A known protected platform the squad cannot counter could therefore be masked by a nearby rifle contact.
implementation: Compute uncountered armour from existing assessed contact index, available AT capability and existing authored-forward policy. No new scan or observation.
Exclude opportunistic close assault when that uncountered threat exists, selecting the original ARMOUR_OVERMATCH branch and exact existing target index.

Existing reposition executor admits the owner-local finite operation; at<=120m it uses existing finite withdrawal, otherwise short screened reposition. Existing cooldown, task, care, reservations, mission and external ownership apply.

Authored forward-order handling unchanged. AT-capable squads retain close-assault option. Mixed crew actor-only elements cannot acquire group reposition/withdrawal; their existing final intent filter yields.

validation.testScope: Extended existing source contract test, no test count increase. Existing physical armour procedure does not establish competing close-infantry priority and remains unrun.

limits: Actual simultaneous-contact decisions, chosen avenues, withdrawal safety, combat balance, HC/JIP and performance UNRUN.
Existing contact classification and knowledge age rules unchanged. No claim that all armour models or ammunition capabilities are balanced.
